heroLead: Wickerham Manor-Fisher is a combined census-designated community in southern Washington County, sitting inside one of the busiest drilling corridors in the state.
intro: It's an unusual name for a place, two older communities folded into one for census purposes, but the mineral ownership underneath it is anything but unusual for this part of Washington County: farm-family land, leased young, held by heirs who now live somewhere else entirely.

We hear from a lot of owners in this exact position, people who inherited an interest tied to a place they've never actually lived, and just want an honest read on whether it's worth holding or selling.

sections.heading: Absentee Ownership Is the Norm Here, Not the Exception
paragraphs: Because Wickerham Manor-Fisher's mineral ownership is so heavily tied to inherited farm parcels, a large share of the interests here are held by people who now live in Pittsburgh, out of state, or further away still. That distance makes it harder to keep track of lease terms, unit changes, and whether a royalty statement is even being calculated correctly.

We handle everything remotely when that's what a family needs, courthouse work, document review, closing, so you're not required to make a trip back to Washington County to sell something you already know you own.

sections.heading: The Deduction Language Buried in Older Leases
paragraphs: Many leases signed in this area during the first leasing wave carry broad post-production deduction language, the kind that lets operators net out gathering, compression, dehydration, and marketing costs before calculating your royalty. Courts have generally upheld that language when it's clearly written, which is part of why so many families here have watched their monthly checks shrink over time without any change in production.
We read every lease we're offered with this in mind, because understanding what's being deducted tells us as much about your interest's value as the production numbers do.

sections.heading: One Payment Instead of a Long, Uneven Tail
paragraphs: A Marcellus well's best production is usually in its first few years, with output declining steadily after that. For an interest already past its early peak, the remaining royalty stream can stretch out for a long time at a shrinking, unpredictable amount. Selling now trades that long tail for a single number you can actually plan around.

faqs.question: I live out of state. Can I sell my Wickerham Manor-Fisher interest without traveling to Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: Yes. We handle the title work through the Washington County recorder of deeds and can close remotely by mail or electronically.

faqs.question: How do you determine my net mineral acres if the deed is unclear?
faqs.answer: We trace the chain of title and cross-reference it against the unit's pooling documents to calculate your actual decimal interest before making an offer.

faqs.question: Do post-production deductions ever violate Pennsylvania law?
faqs.answer: The Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act sets a one-eighth net floor, so deductions are generally legal as long as your check stays above that floor. We can help you understand what's being deducted from yours.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to get started?
faqs.answer: A copy of your lease and any recent royalty statements are the most useful starting point, but we can locate most records ourselves if you don't have them.
